text:
linh: heads up — noticed client-id duplication causing quota fragmentation on /v1/generate. example: same caller sent client_id as query and X-Client-Id header, counted as two tenants.

sam: can you paste a minimal request + route config?

linh: request example: `GET /v1/generate?client_id=svc-123&prompt=...` with header `X-Client-Id: svc-456`. route: `service: inference; match: /v1/generate` — our current rewrites inject `x-client-id` but we also preserve query params, so quota lookup sometimes uses query->tenant and header->tenant separately.

matthew: ugh. two problems: precedence for where tenant comes from, and what ends up in cache key. if we canonicalize to header but leave query param, caches still split.

sara: my vote: do minimal breaking change — prefer header when present, but strip `client_id` query param before cache key calculation. default behaviour: prefer header, fallback to query param.

aja: agreed on ordering. we should also make rule ordering explicit in the rewrite config (so console + API don't implicitly reorder). propose adding `priority` to rules and a clear list: 1) path clean (normalize slashes, remove ../), 2) strip sensitive query params, 3) header injection/override, 4) cache key calculation.

linh: sketch of a rule i put together:
```yaml
- id: tenant-from-header-or-query
  priority: 100
  match:
    path: /v1/generate
  actions:
    - set_header:
        name: X-Client-Id
        from: header:X-Client-Id
        fallback: query:client_id
    - remove_query_params: [client_id]
    - note: "ensure cache key excludes removed params"
```

sam: looks good. two notes: (1) `from: header:` must be case-insensitive for header name, (2) need telemetry when fallback is used so we can audit how many calls rely on query param. metric names?

matthew: propose metrics: `rewrite.rule.applied{rule_id=...,route=...}` and `rewrite.rule.fallback_used{rule_id=...,fallback=...}`. also `rewrite.conflict.{route,...}` if two rules try to set same header.

aja: console UX: we need to expose `priority` in the rule editor and surface preview of final request (show computed path, headers, query after applying rules). really helps non-engineering customers to understand behaviour.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: rewrite-config v2 -> canary (2%)

ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: canary rollout active in us-west-2 (2% traffic). :rocket:

sam: thanks, can we also add a quick e2e test for this flow in the routing test harness? i.e., input request with header+query -> assert header becomes canonical, query param removed, cache key stable.

linh: yep i'll open a PR with the YAML + tests + telemetry. adding @sam @aja for review.

sara: i'll take console changes (preview + priority control) — will prototype mockups tomorrow.

matthew: i'll wire the metrics and add an alert for sudden increase in `rewrite.rule.fallback_used` (signal of client regressions).

linh: great. thanks all. will follow up with PR link shortly. :thumbsup:
